On May 10, 2026 , the Stadio Ennio Tardini hosted a Serie A encounter that would test the resolve of both Parma and AS Roma . With European ambitions and local pride on the line, the two sides engaged in a tactical battle that evolved into a chaotic and thrilling spectacle. Roman Dominance and the Opening Goal AS Roma started the match with clear intent, dominating possession and forcing Parma to defend deep. After a few early offside calls disrupted their rhythm, the visitors finally broke the deadlock in the 22nd minute. Donyell Malen showcased his clinical nature, receiving a pass from Manu Koné and, following an assist by Paulo Dybala , unleashing a powerful strike from outside the box that beat Zion Suzuki . The goal was a just reward for Roma's early dominance, as they controlled 66% of the ball during the opening period. Parma's Resurgence and a Second-Half Turnaround The narrative shifted immediately after the restart. In the 47th minute, Parma stunned the visitors when Hans Nicolussi Caviglia set up Gabriel Strefezza , who finished accurately with his right foot to level the score. The goal ignited the home crowd, and although Strefezza earned a yellow card for his exuberant celebrations, the momentum had firmly swung in Parma's favor. As the game entered its final stages, the tension reached a breaking point. In the 87th minute, it appeared that Parma had secured a famous comeback victory. Nahuel Estévez provided the crucial assist for Mandela Keita , who found the back of the net to put the hosts ahead 2-1. However, the drama was far from over as the match entered an extraordinary period of stoppage time. Stoppage-Time Chaos and the Decisive Penalty In the 94th minute, AS Roma clawed their way back into the game when Devyne Rensch struck a brilliant long-range effort following a pass from Daniele Ghilardi to make it 2-2. The drama intensified in the 99th minute when a VAR check identified a shirt-pull by Sascha Britschgi on Rensch inside the area. The referee awarded a penalty and showed Britschgi a second yellow card, sending him for an early bath. In the 11th minute of added time, Donyell Malen stepped up to the spot. Despite Zion Suzuki getting a hand to the ball, the power of the strike carried it into the net. This final twist ensured AS Roma left the Tardini with all three points, leaving the home side heartbroken after a valiant display.

Early Dominance and the Opening Blow On May 5, 2026, Roma sought to dictate the tempo from the opening whistle, controlling a staggering 66% of possession. Their patience was rewarded in the 22nd minute when Donyell Malen broke the deadlock. After slick buildup play involving Manu Kone and an assist from Paulo Dybala , Malen unleashed a powerful strike from outside the box that beat the keeper. The home side continued to press, but despite their territorial advantage, they headed into the interval with only a slender one-goal lead over Parma Calcio 1913 . Parma’s Resurgence and Late Drama The second half began with a shock for the hosts as Parma leveled the score in the 47th minute. Gabriel Strefezza found the net following a clinical pass from Hans Nicolussi Caviglia . matches.description: Watch AS Roma vs Lazio highlights and goals from Serie A on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 17, 2026. The Stadio Olimpico crackled with anticipation on May 17, 2026 , as AS Roma and Lazio prepared to write the latest chapter in their historic Serie A rivalry. Mancini Rises to the Occasion The match began with the high-octane intensity expected of a Derby della Capitale, with both sides trading tactical blows in a cagey opening period. The deadlock was finally broken in the 40th minute when AS Roma exploited their strength from set-pieces. Niccolo Pisilli delivered a pinpoint corner from the left, finding the forehead of Gianluca Mancini , who powered his header home. There was a brief moment of silence as VAR checked the goal's validity, but the referee eventually pointed to the center circle to confirm the lead. Tempers flared shortly after, with Mario Hermoso and Matteo Cancellieri both receiving yellow cards for unsportsmanlike conduct as the first half drew to a close. Double Delight and Lazio Discipline Crumbles Roma continued to apply pressure in the second half, and the script repeated itself in the 66th minute. This time, it was Paulo Dybala who provided the ammunition from a corner on the left, swinging a dangerous ball into the box for Gianluca Mancini to once again outleap the defense and head into the net. The momentum shifted even more dramatically in the 70th minute when the match descended into chaos. Following an outbreak of violent conduct, the referee issued straight red cards to both Wesley and Nicolo Rovella , leaving Lazio to navigate the final twenty minutes with only nine men on the pitch. Late Woodwork and Closing Stages Despite being two men down, Lazio attempted to remain compact, but AS Roma pushed for a third to put the game completely out of reach. Artem Dovbyk , introduced as a substitute for Dybala , came agonisingly close in the 89th minute when his well-struck effort rattled the post. In the dying embers of the game, Matias Soule forced a save from Alessio Furlanetto , and Jan Ziolkowski saw a header fly wide. As the final whistle blew, the Giallorossi celebrated a hard-fought victory defined by Mancini's aerial dominance and a total disciplinary collapse from their cross-town rivals.

The stage was set on May 24, 2026 , for a gripping Serie A fixture as Hellas Verona hosted AS Roma in a match that promised tactical intrigue and high stakes. A Tightly Contested First Half Throughout the opening forty-five minutes, the match unfolded as a strategic standoff. AS Roma looked to orchestrate attacks through the creative vision of Paulo Dybala , whose repeated corner kicks kept the pressure on the Verona backline. Despite the visitors' intent, the home side remained disciplined, effectively neutralizing scoring threats. Verona attempted to find their own rhythm, with Kieron Bowie testing the waters from distance, but neither side could find the breakthrough before the referee signaled the end of the first half. The Second Half Turning Point The complexion of the game shifted dramatically early in the second half when Verona's Nicolas Valentini was dismissed following a second yellow card, forcing his side to navigate the remainder of the match with ten men. Capitalizing on the numerical advantage, AS Roma earned a penalty after a VAR review confirmed a handball by Kieron Bowie . Although Donyell Malen saw his initial spot-kick blocked, he reacted quickly to tuck away the rebound. The visitors controlled the tempo thereafter, eventually cementing their victory in stoppage time when Stephan El Shaarawy converted an assist from Paulo Dybala to round off a disciplined performance.
